title: Scenic Sri Lanka
summary: Eleven private days from the Sigiriya rock fortress to Yala National Park, ending with the slow part of the south coast.

The south coast in the afternoon

facts.detail: Kandy · Cultural Triangle · Sigiriya · Yala · Tangalle · Galle
December to April on this route, when the south coast is dry

includes.heading: What the journey includes.
includes.body: Everything below is arranged before you land, so the days ask nothing of you beyond turning up. Flights and visas sit outside the plan, and we will say so clearly in the proposal.

items.title: Accommodation
items.body: Ten nights, chosen for where they sit rather than how many stars they carry. A lake house in Kandy, a tented camp near the park, a fort room in Galle.

items.title: Activities
items.body: Guided walks, two safaris, the climbs at Sigiriya and Dambulla, and whatever you want to add once we have talked.

items.title: Meals
items.body: Breakfast every day, plus the meals that are part of a stay or a long drive. The rest stays open, because eating out is half the trip.

items.title: Transfers and driver
items.body: Airport pick-up and drop-off, and the same driver and vehicle for the whole route, so you are not starting again every morning.

itinerary.heading: The island, at your pace.
itinerary.lede: Open a day to see what it holds and where you sleep.

days.title: A City Around a Lake
days.body: A gentle first day. The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic in the late afternoon, the Royal Botanical Gardens if you have the energy, and a viewpoint above the lake at dusk. Your driver meets you at the airport and the drive up is the first part of the trip, not a transfer to get through.

stay.name: Myst by Cinnamon
stay.note: Hillside rooms above the city, ten minutes from the temple.

days.title: Into the Cultural Triangle
days.body: Two days of old ground. Dambulla’s golden cave temples early, before the heat and the crowds, then a slow cycle through the royal ruins of Polonnaruwa with a guide who can tell you what you are looking at.

stay.name: Jetwing Lake
stay.note: Low, quiet and built around the water, with the ruins within easy reach.

days.title: The Rock That Rises From the Plain
days.body: Climb the 200-metre fortress at first light for one of the great views in Asia. If the queue looks long, neighbouring Pidurangala gives you the rock itself framed against the sky, which is arguably the better photograph.

stay.name: Sigiriya King’s Resort
stay.note: Close enough for a dawn start without a drive in the dark.

days.title: The Dry Zone at Its Most Dramatic
days.body: Three days of scrub, granite and lagoon, with leopards, elephants and birdlife on morning and afternoon safaris. We keep one safari a day rather than two, so the middle of the day belongs to you.

stay.name: DoubleTree by Hilton
stay.note: A short run from the park gate, with a pool for the hours between drives.

days.title: The Coast Arrives Like an Exhale
days.body: The drive south ends at wide, quiet beaches. Nothing is scheduled. The Hummanaya blow hole is nearby if you want a reason to leave the sand.

stay.name: Anantara Peace Haven
stay.note: On its own headland above the water, with a path down to the beach.

days.title: The Old Fort by the Ocean
days.body: Ramparts, galleries and a lighthouse at the point. One day for the fort and its history, one for the beach, with dinner inside the walls when the day tourists have gone.

stay.name: Jetwing Lighthouse
stay.note: Just outside the walls, with the sea on three sides.

photos.caption: The way down from the hills

days.title: The Full Sweep Behind You
days.body: A private transfer to Colombo airport, with time built in for the traffic. Eleven days, six regions, and one route that never doubled back on itself.

stay.name: Private transfer
stay.note: Colombo airport, timed to your flight.

timeAnswer: Eleven days covers this route without rushing. Shorter trips usually mean dropping a region rather than moving faster.
